item.title: Nonintegrability theorem on perturbed integrable Hamiltonian dynamical systems with two independent resonances
item.description: arXiv:2611.04962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we establish a new theorem for nonintegrability of a perturbed, autonomous, two-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian dynamical system with two independent resonances, based on a criterion which utilizes the well-known theorem of Poincar\'e and a Lie-series symplectic transformation. We also make certain assumptions and suggestions as to when the theorem holds and when it does not.
item.dc:creator: Nikos Zafeiriadis, Efthymia Meletlidou, Christos Efthymiopoulos, Christos Volos

item.title: Modal interactions in strongly nonlinear coupled oscillators with closely spaced modes and nonclassical damping distribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.05125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear and nonlinear mechanical structures with closely spaced modes and non-classical (nonproportional) damping distribution are susceptible to modal interactions with energy exchanges between modes. In this work we analyze these interactions in a two-degree-of-freedom (2 DoF) coupled oscillator subject to impulse excitation, utilizing action-angle variables and the method of multiple scales. To show the basic steps of the methodology we start from the linear system, then proceed to analyze modal interactions in the system with strongly nonlinear cubic stiffness nonlinearity. In contrast to the linear case, once the dynamics of the nonlinear system is captured in 1:1 resonance, strongly nonlinear modal interactions occur depending on energy. These regimes as well as attraction to capture, 1:1 capture and escape from capture are analyzed in detail. Our analytical study determines the ranges of parameter values for which nonlinear modal interactions due to resonance capture occur. The analytical predictions are fully verified by direct numerical simulations of the governing equations of motion. Possible extensions of the present work to systems of oscillators with more DoF and other types of dissipative elements, e.g., friction or hysteresis are discussed.
item.dc:creator: C. A. Hubay, T. Kalmar-Nagy, L. Bergman, A. F. Vakakis

item.title: Designing turbulence through hierarchies
item.description: arXiv:2611.04706v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Turbulence is defined by a set of emergent and singular phenomena: a constant-flux energy cascade, intermittency, a dissipation rate that survives the vanishing of viscosity, and the spontaneous loss of determinism of the inviscid limit. Which physical ingredients produce them remains unclear, because in fluids they always come together with incompressibility, spatial structure and vortex dynamics. Here we show that a hierarchy of inertia, coupled by the purely geometric nonlinearity of rigid constraints, is enough. A planar chain of rigid pendula whose lengths and masses decrease geometrically, coupled only through nearest-neighbor constraints, develops a far-from-equilibrium cascade that replaces thermal equipartition, with statistically local and time-irreversible energy transfer despite intrinsically nonlocal coupling. Its fluctuations are intermittent, yet self-similarity is restored by a hidden scale symmetry. As the viscosity vanishes, the dissipation rate saturates at a finite value, and thermal noise consistent with fluctuation-dissipation balance is amplified from the smallest to the largest scales within a fraction of a large-scale period. Because the hierarchy can be tuned and the same dynamics can be realized mechanically or electrically, turbulence becomes a property that can be designed and measured in the laboratory.
item.dc:creator: Flavio Tuteri, Andr\'e Freitas

item.title: Symbol sequences from three-rotor coincidences and their word-complexity
item.description: arXiv:2606.25766v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the three-rotor problem, three equally massive point particles move on a circle interacting via attractive pairwise cosine potentials. Rotors can represent superconducting phases of metallic segments in a chain of coupled Josephson junctions. We propose a digitization of the classical dynamics that records successive pair and triple coincidences of rotors using four symbols. Rotor coincidences correspond to boundaries in a disjoint partition of the configuration torus into cells where the rotors are ordered clockwise and anticlockwise. It is shown that isolated rotor coincidences must be crossings. Despite being a rather coarse digitization, we find that replacing trajectories by coincidence symbol sequences captures significant qualitative features of the dynamics through word statistics. Word-complexity $C_n$ measures the diversity of $n$-letter words in the symbol sequence while topological entropy governs asymptotic exponential growth of $C_n$. Sequences from periodic orbits have a word-complexity that saturates at the period. Ultra-high-energy trajectories with irrational `slope' are quasiperiodic. We show that they have zero entropy and $C_n = n+3$ by examining limiting slopes and by a mapping to Sturmian sequences. We examine their grammar rules and propose how their right-special words may be identified. On the other hand, numerical investigation of sequences from globally chaotic orbits leads us to conjecture an exponentially growing word-complexity $C_n = 3 \times 2^{n-1}$ with a topological entropy $\log 2$. We identify grammar rules that imply this conjectured word-complexity and model the resulting sequences as a subshift of finite type, unlike those at ultra-high energies which are not topological Markov chains.
item.dc:creator: Govind S. Krishnaswami, Anirudh Rameshan

item.title: Dynamics and non-integrability of the Swinging Atwood Machine with a massive string: chaos, periodic orbits and resonance structures
item.description: arXiv:2608.09310v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Building upon our previous studies on nonlinear variable-length pendulum systems, we investigate the Swinging Atwood Machine with a massive string. In contrast to the classical model, string inertia introduces a configuration-dependent moment of inertia, leading to a modified Hamiltonian structure and substantially richer dynamics. To uncover the global organization of the phase space, we combine Poincar\'e sections, bifurcation diagrams, and Lyapunov exponent maps with our recently developed numerical framework ,,Lyapunov Refined Maps". This approach provides a unified visualization of periodic, quasi-periodic, chaotic, and terminating motions, revealing intricate resonance networks and high-order periodic structures. We investigate the influence of the string mass, system parameters, and energy by constructing Lyapunov maps in parameter and initial-condition spaces and on fixed-energy surfaces. Liouville integrability is studied within the Morales-Ramis theory. By analyzing the normal variational equations along explicit non-stationary radial solutions and applying the Kovacic algorithm, we prove that the differential Galois group is generically SL(2,C), providing a rigorous obstruction to meromorphic Liouville integrability for every nonzero string mass. Thus, the exceptional integrable case of the classical Swinging Atwood Machine is destroyed by the inclusion of string inertia.
item.dc:creator: Wojciech Szumi\'nski, Jakub Bembenek

item.title: Hierarchical Decoupling of Informational and Energetic Channels in Dissipative Chaos: From Microscopic Tangles to Macroscopic Transport
item.description: arXiv:2608.19620v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Characterizing deterministic chaos in driven dissipative systems presents a fundamental challenge: geometric methods detect topological horseshoes ($h_T > 0$) without certifying physical measures, while macroscopic observables reduce multi-scale dynamics into low-dimensional indicators. We demonstrate that phase-space contraction structurally decouples the informational channel, governed by topological complexity and Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy ($h_{KS}$), from the energetic channel governing macroscopic dissipation, power balance, and transport. We establish a three-tier hierarchical architecture bridging: (I) microscopic topology (invariant manifold tangles), (II) ergodic physical measures (metric entropy and Lyapunov spectra), and (III) macroscopic ensemble statistics (variance and transport flux). In the forced two-well Duffing oscillator, high-resolution numerical analyses reveal the origin of classical predictive failures: dense homoclinic tangles degenerate into non-retaining transient saddles ($h_T > 0, h_{KS} = 0$) collapsing to periodic sinks, whereas macroscopic chaos persists past primary homoclinic tangency via higher-order saddle relays. Generalizing to periodic-potential rotational systems shows that heteroclinic crossings and resonant Shapiro steps enforce geometric bounds on phase slips and transport. Structurally disentangling informational capacity from energetic realization connects geometric mechanics with non-equilibrium statistical observability, offering a new diagnostic framework for noise-induced instabilities in nonlinear systems.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Hikihara

item.title: Forecasting Low-Dimensional Navier-Stokes equations via Multi-Dimensional Hybrid Quantum Reservoir Computing
item.description: arXiv:2509.04006v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The prediction of complex dynamics remains an open problem across many domains of physics, where nonlinearities and multiscale interactions severely limit the reliability of conventional forecasting methods. Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for information processing by exploiting the high dimensionality of the Hilbert space, where the dynamics of quantum systems take place. Here, we introduce a hybrid quantum-classical reservoir architecture capable of handling multivariate time series through quantum evolution combined with classical memory enhancement. Our model employs a five-qubit transverse-field Ising Hamiltonian with input-modulated dynamics and temporal multiplexing, enabling the encoding of input signals over multiple timescales. We apply this framework to two paradigmatic models of chaotic behavior in fluid dynamics, where multiscale dynamics and nonlinearities play a dominant role: a low-dimensional truncation of the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations and the Lorenz-63 system. By systematically scanning the quantum system's parameter space, we identify regions that maximize forecasting performance, as measured by the Valid Prediction Time. The observed robustness and reliable performances for both dynamical systems suggest that this hybrid quantum approach offers a flexible platform for modelling complex nonlinear time series.
item.dc:creator: L. Salatino, L. Mariani, A. Giordano, F. D'Amore, C. Mastroianni, L. Pontieri, A. Vinci, C. Gencarelli, L. Primavera, F. Plastina, J. Settino, F. Carbone

item.title: Measurement and feedback-driven adaptive dynamics in the classical and quantum kicked top
item.description: arXiv:2604.19874v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In classical dynamical systems, stochastic feedback can stabilize otherwise unstable periodic orbits, giving rise to distinct controlled and uncontrolled phases as the rate of control application is varied. In this work, we apply these control protocols in classical, semiclassical, and quantum regimes to the kicked top, a paradigmatic model of quantum chaos. The quantum kicked top, modeled as the dynamics of a spin-S object, naturally interpolates between these regimes with the spin size S acting as an effective Planck constant. We show that the dynamics of the kicked top in classical, semiclassical, and fully quantum limits can all be controlled using stochastic feedback protocols. Comparing the full quantum dynamics to a truncated Wigner approximation that captures quantum noise but neglects interference beyond the Ehrenfest time, we find that low-moment observables are largely accounted for semiclassically, while higher moments retain a discrepancy that peaks at the control transition, consistent with contributions from interference and possibly nonlinearities in rare trajectories that explore the compact phase space. We also find rapid purification in the numerics studied for all rates of control considered, suggesting that control quenches the top's ability to encode a qubit of quantum information even in the uncontrolled phase.
item.dc:creator: Mahaveer Prasad, Ahana Chakraborty, Thomas Iadecola, Manas Kulkarni, J. H. Pixley, Sriram Ganeshan, Justin H. Wilson

item.title: Score-Based Modeling of Effective Langevin Dynamics with State-Dependent Mobility
item.description: arXiv:2604.23952v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In a previous work [L. T. Giorgini, Phys. Rev. E 114, L012102 (2026)], we introduced stochastic reduced-order models that reproduce by construction the stationary density and short-time correlations of the observed variables, using a constant mobility matrix and the score, the gradient of the logarithm of this density. Here we generalize the framework to state-dependent mobilities, calibrated so that the model also reproduces the finite-lag correlation functions of chosen target observables. The calibration uses exact finite-lag forms of the generalized fluctuation-dissipation theorem, which express time derivatives of lagged correlations as averages over observed pairs of states and are linear in the mobility. When the mobility is expanded on a basis of known fields, its coefficients follow from a least-squares problem involving only the stationary score, and the observables and basis are selected by data-driven diagnostics. Otherwise, a neural-network mobility is calibrated through the conditional score of the finite-time transition density. We validate the approach analytically on a Cox-Ingersoll-Ross process and numerically on a two-dimensional nonequilibrium diffusion with multiplicative noise and a 36-dimensional soft-spin Landau-Lifshitz chain. Both methods reproduce the stationary statistics and the target correlations accurately. Because the identities can be integrated between consecutive lags, so that no time derivatives need to be estimated, the recovered drift and diffusion are much less sensitive to coarse sampling than Kramers-Moyal estimates, which require short sampling intervals. Calibration requires no simulation of the model and applies to high-dimensional systems.
item.dc:creator: Ludovico T. Giorgini
